title: BioChirp: federated retrieval over 26 biomedical databases with provenance, MCP integration, and a token-budget-aware planner
description: BioChirp is a federated biomedical retrieval system that aggregates 26 curated databases (BioGRID, STRING, OmniPath, Orphanet, ChEMBL, ClinVar, HPO, Reactome, WikiPathways, MSigDB, DGIdb, DrugCentral, TTD, PharmGKB, HGNC, …) into a unified retrieval interface. Each returned row carries verifiable per-DB provenance (db_version + db_snapshot_date). The release contains: (1) a 75K-edge knowledge graph with 100% provenance coverage and explicit cross-DB epistemic-uncertainty edges (AGREE / DISAGREE / UNIQUE); (2) an MCP server suite (27 servers, 72 tools) installable as a PyPI package, a one-click DXT bundle, or a hosted HTTP/SSE endpoint; (3) a token-budget-aware federated retrieval planner formalised as a Multiple-Choice Knapsack with priorities, with greedy achieving empirical mean competitive ratio 0.9998 against the DP optimum on a 90-instance benchmark; (4) a paper-grade evaluation harness measuring structured-output recall, provenance fidelity, and reproducibility kappa across multiple LLM baselines.
